<reason>Side B (PRO) prevailed by exposing a fatal contradiction in Side A's case: if platforms cannot authenticate clothing due to lack of unique identifiers, ordinary buyers cannot be the "least-cost avoiders" either. Side A conceded buyers can only perform "sanity checks" against obvious fakes ([A2.1]), undermining their argument that buyers are best positioned to bear counterfeit risk. Side B also neutralized Side A's economic fears by distinguishing scalable digital screening from costly physical authentication for every item, and by noting counterfeiters target recognizable brands rather than obscure vintage pieces. Side B maintained sharper rebuttals and clearer weighing of information asymmetry and incentives.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 1 ([B2.1]) exposing the contradiction between Side A's claims that platforms cannot authenticate clothing and that buyers are the least-cost avoiders, which Side A failed to fully resolve despite later conceding buyers can only perform "sanity checks."</best_rebuttal>
